vocabulary.meaning_en: an amount or number of something (not exact); used in positive sentences and offers
vocabulary.example: I would like some money, please.

vocabulary.meaning_en: used in negative sentences, general questions and with "if"

vocabulary.example: I'm hungry. I want something to eat.

vocabulary.meaning_en: any thing at all (negatives and questions)
vocabulary.example: I don't want anything to eat.

vocabulary.meaning_en: at any time; whenever you want
vocabulary.example: Anytime you're in town, come and visit me.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (of a sentence) not negative; saying yes
vocabulary.example: "I want some tea" is a positive sentence.
"I don't want any tea" is a negative sentence.

vocabulary.meaning_en: ask if someone wants something you can give
an open question where we don't expect a special answer
vocabulary.example: "Have you seen anyone at school?" is a general question.
You look hungry. Would you like some food?

vocabulary.meaning_en: something that does not follow the rule
vocabulary.example: There are exceptions to every English rule.

fine_lines.title: some vs any
fine_lines.explanation_ar: some في الجمل المثبتة وفي الأسئلة التي نعرض فيها شيئًا أو نطلبه أو نتوقع فيها الجواب نعم. any في الجمل المنفية والأسئلة العامة ومع if.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Some": positive sentences, and questions where we offer, ask for something, or expect "yes". "Any": negative sentences, general questions, and with "if".

fine_lines.title: something vs anything
fine_lines.explanation_ar: I want something to eat (مثبت). I don't want anything to eat (منفي). لا نقول I don't want something.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "I want something to eat" (positive). "I don't want anything to eat" (negative). Not "I don't want something".

examples.sentence: I don't want anything to drink.

fine_lines.title: someone vs anyone in questions
fine_lines.explanation_ar: Have you seen anyone? سؤال عام مفتوح. Is someone looking for me? سؤال نتوقع فيه الجواب نعم.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Have you seen anyone?" is a general, open question. "Is someone looking for me?" expects a yes answer.

examples.sentence: Did you see anyone at school today?

expressions.example: You look hungry. Would you like some food?
Has anybody seen my shoes? I can't find them.

expressions.phrase: If anybody wants help, let me know.
expressions.meaning_ar: إذا احتاج أيّ أحد المساعدة فأخبروني.
expressions.meaning_en: Tell me if any person needs help.
expressions.example: If anybody wants help with the homework, let me know.

expressions.phrase: Anytime you're in town, come and visit me.
expressions.meaning_ar: متى كنت في المدينة، تعال وزرني.
expressions.meaning_en: Whenever you are in my city, visit me.
expressions.example: Anytime you're in town, come and visit me.

expressions.meaning_en: You can phone me whenever you want.
expressions.example: If you need help, give me a call anytime.

grammar.title: some in positive sentences, any in negative sentences
grammar.explanation_ar: في الجملة المثبتة نستعمل some (و something / someone). في الجملة المنفية نستعمل any (و anything / anyone).
grammar.explanation_en: In positive sentences use some (something, someone). In negative sentences use any (anything, anyone).
examples: I'm hungry. I want something to eat.
I don't want anything to eat.

grammar.title: Questions: any for general questions, some for offers and requests
grammar.explanation_ar: في السؤال العام الذي لا نعرض فيه شيئًا ولا نتوقع نعم، نستعمل any. أما إذا كنا نعرض شيئًا أو نطلبه أو نتوقع الجواب نعم فنستعمل some.
grammar.explanation_en: In a general question (no offer, no special answer expected), use any. When you offer, ask for something, or expect "yes", use some.
examples: Can I have some water, please?

grammar.title: any with if (and the idea of if)
grammar.explanation_ar: مع if نستعمل any عادةً، خاصة عندما لا يهمنا من هو أو متى: If anybody wants help, let me know. وكلمة anytime تحمل معنى if: Anytime you're in town = If you are in town.
grammar.explanation_en: With "if" we usually use any, especially when it doesn't matter who or when: "If anybody wants help, let me know." "Anytime" carries the idea of if: "Anytime you're in town" = "If you are in town".
examples: If anybody calls, take a message.
Anytime you want, give me a call.

grammar.title: someone, anyone, somebody, anybody are singular
grammar.explanation_ar: هذه الكلمات مفردة وتأخذ فعلًا مفردًا: Someone is here. Has anyone seen it?
grammar.explanation_en: These words are singular and take a singular verb: "Someone is here." "Has anyone seen it?"

grammar.title: James's 80% rule
grammar.explanation_ar: هذه قواعد عامة صحيحة في معظم الحالات، وقد تجد استثناءات (مثل: If you want some, take it).
grammar.explanation_en: These are general rules that work most of the time. You may find exceptions (e.g. "If you want some, take it").
examples: If you'd like some tea, just ask.

questions.question: "You look hungry. Would you like ___ food?"
questions.explanation_en: An offer, we expect yes: some.

questions.question: "___ you're in town, come and visit me."
Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation_ar: النفي مع any، و someone مفرد.
questions.explanation_en: Negative takes any; someone is singular.
